title: SHIFT(hold) + NUMBER not working to switch between Fancy zones personal layouts
author: ed-ferreira

status.label: Intentional shortcut change
status.detail: PR #48569 deliberately changed layout switching during a drag to require Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit so stale drag state cannot steal ordinary number keys; two later commenters independently confirm the old gesture no longer works.

next_action.label: Explain current behavior
next_action.reason: Clarify that this is an intentional safety change rather than request diagnostics for a known code path.

judgment.rationale: The reported loss of Shift/secondary-click + digit switching matches an intentional behavior change merged in #48569, not an unexplained regression requiring a bug design.
evidence: Two reporters confirm that digits no longer switch layouts during a drag on 0.101.2362.
A third commenter confirms the shortcut issue and separately reports Explorer placement and last-zone symptoms.
A fourth commenter confirms the same behavior on 0.101.2362.
Current FancyZones.cpp requires Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit both while dragging and not dragging.
Merged PR #48569 states that the stricter chord prevents stuck drag state from stealing number keys, referencing root symptom #410.
judgment.recommended_action: Post a maintainer-direction comment explaining the intentional change and direct any request for an alternative safe gesture to a feature discussion.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones no longer accepts bare digits while a window is being dragged; users now must use Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit to switch quick layouts.
known_information: The old Shift-drag and secondary-mouse activation workflows allowed a digit to select a quick layout.
The behavior changed in PowerToys 0.101.2362 and is confirmed by three additional reporters.
A third commenter confirmed the shortcut concern while also describing separate Explorer placement and last-zone behavior.
Merged PR #48569 intentionally requires Win+Ctrl+Alt during a drag to prevent ordinary number keys from being swallowed when drag state is stale.
inferences: Users may still benefit from a safer configurable drag-time gesture, but restoring bare-digit handling would reintroduce the input-safety risk addressed by #48569.
issue_context.analysis: Repository history resolves the shortcut regression: the current behavior is deliberate and covered by an explicit safety tradeoff in the merged PR. The newly mentioned placement symptoms should be investigated separately rather than folded into this shortcut decision.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full issue and both comments; no linked fix or assignee exists.
Inspected FancyZones.cpp lines handling quickLayoutSwitch and traced the change with git blame to commit dd26d86580.
Reviewed merged PR #48569, which documents the reason, implementation, and validation for requiring Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit during drags.
Re-read the full live body and discussion through 2026-09-02T20:49:50Z; the newest confirmation reinforces the same interaction concern but adds no contradictory maintainer decision.

actions.label: Explain intentional shortcut change

comment.body:
Thanks for the confirmations. The Shift/secondary-click + bare number-key behavior changed intentionally in #48569: FancyZones now requires Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit for quick layout switching even while dragging, because accepting bare digits whenever FancyZones believed a drag was active could steal normal number-key input when drag state became stuck. Restoring the old bare-digit gesture would reintroduce that risk.

The Explorer placement and last-used-zone behavior mentioned above sound like separate FancyZones issues from this shortcut change. If those still reproduce on the latest build, please open separate focused issues for them with exact reproduction steps and, if possible, add a fresh `/bugreport` immediately after reproducing so those symptoms can be investigated independently.
